h: Ally Pally tips for a treetop day
p: A Go Ape course takes longer than many people expect. Allow a good couple of hours or more for the course itself, plus extra time for arriving, checking in and the safety briefing, which you'll need to listen to properly. Once you're up in the trees, the instructors are on the ground keeping an eye out, so you'll be clipping and unclipping yourself along the way.

Younger participants need a participating adult with them, with set ratios depending on ages, so check what applies to your group before booking. Bring a water bottle and a snack for afterwards, and wear clothes you don't mind getting a bit grubby.

Getting there is straightforward. Alexandra Palace station, on the line from Moorgate and King's Cross, is at the foot of the park, and buses climb the hill to the palace itself. Wood Green on the Piccadilly line isn't far either. The climb up to the palace is steep, so allow time if you're walking.

There's much more to do once you've come down from the trees. The palace has an ice rink that's open to the public, and the boating lake in the park is popular in the warmer months. The view from the terrace in front of the palace stretches right across London, and it's a cracking free viewpoint. On the eastern side of the park there's a pitch and putt course, and the park's open spaces are perfect for a picnic or a kickabout.
